g.text: The foreign-born share rose in 43 of 51 rich countries since 1990. Israel's fell the most, from 36% to 22%,

text.style: font-size: 13.5px; font-family: 'Inter'; fill: #4a4741

g.text: even though 29% more immigrants live there now. The Baltic states fell too, for the opposite reason.

text.style: font-weight: 500; font-size: 10.5px; font-family: 'IBM Plex Mono'; text-anchor: start; fill: #e4572e
font-weight: 600; font-size: 13px; font-family: 'Inter'; text-anchor: start; fill: #17171a

g.text: Foreign-born share of the population, 51 high-income countries

text.style: font-size: 10.5px; font-family: 'Inter'; text-anchor: start; fill: #4a4741

g.text: Red: Israel. Blue: the Baltic states. Grey: other countries where the share fell.

text.style: font-weight: 500; font-size: 10.5px; font-family: 'IBM Plex Mono'; text-anchor: start; fill: #e4572e
font-weight: 600; font-size: 13px; font-family: 'Inter'; text-anchor: start; fill: #17171a

g.text: Two ways to fall: more natives, or fewer immigrants

text.style: font-size: 10.5px; font-family: 'Inter'; text-anchor: start; fill: #4a4741

g.text: People living in each country, millions. Israel's immigrants rose; Latvia's fell by two-thirds.

text.style: font-size: 8px; font-family: 'IBM Plex Mono'; fill: #8c877d

g.text: DATA UN DESA International Migrant Stock 2024, via Our World in Data. World Bank income groups, 2025.

text.style: font-size: 8px; font-family: 'IBM Plex Mono'; fill: #8c877d

g.text: NOTE Foreign-born includes people of foreign citizenship where birthplace isn't recorded. Population

text.style: font-size: 8px; font-family: 'IBM Plex Mono'; fill: #8c877d

g.text: is the UN migrant count divided by the UN migrant share. Countries with 1 million people or more.

text.style: font-weight: 500; font-size: 9px; font-family: 'IBM Plex Mono'; text-anchor: end; fill: #17171a
